summary: Async embed batching order rotation causing non-repeatable rerank results for customer AtlasSearch
description: Issue summary: Customer reports inconsistent rerank top-k across repeated queries when embedding ingestion uses async batching. Impact: Search results non-deterministic (top-k changes between identical queries), intermittent high tail-latency on rerank requests causing user-visible flakiness. Environment: AtlasSearch on Dedicated (us-west-2), ingest path using async-embed-ingest service with batching window 200ms. Observed since 2026-02-27 after ingest pipeline change that gated batch rotation optimization. Expected: Deterministic rerank ordering for identical query+corpus, and consistent latency within SLA.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Upload corpus of ~50k docs via customer's async bulk ingest (batch_size ~ 512, windows=200ms). 2) Pin embeddings to redwood-embed-v2 and reranker to redwood-rerank-small. 3) Issue same rerank query (same prompt, same candidate vector set) 10x within 60s. 4) Observe top-10 variance and occasional 5xx/timeout on rerank calls. 5) Re-run after changing ingest to sync path; variance disappears.
observed_behavior: - Non-deterministic top-k rerank output between runs. - Occasionally rerank returns fewer than requested k results. - Tail latency spikes > 2x normal during warmup of rotated batches. - Some rerank calls fallback to CPU path generating higher latency and score drift.
expected_behavior: - Stable top-k ordering for identical inputs. - No increased tail latency due to ingest batching. - No silent fallback to CPU at normal load.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: batch_rotation optimization reorders embeddings across replicas leading to non-stable candidate ordering which, combined with KV-cache misses and intermittent CPU fallback, produces non-repeatability. Findings: - Reproducer shows variance only when async batching enabled. - Trace shows batch-id included in rerank request metadata; ordering not normalized before scoring. - Embed worker reported occasional partial-commit for last minibatch resulting in fewer candidate vectors for rerank. - No evidence of model weight drift. - Related PR applied to change batch rotation commit strategy (see related_github_prs).
customer_communication: 2026-03-01: Customer reported via support email with sample query and corpus. 2026-03-02: Support acknowledged and requested logs/trace ids. 2026-03-04: Shared workaround to switch to sync ingest. 2026-03-08: Customer confirmed workaround removed variance but requested fix for async mode to avoid throughput regression.
workaround: Advise customer to route critical rerank pipelines to sync ingest or set async batch window to 0 (falls back to sync behavior). This reduces throughput but restores determinism.
resolution: Mitigation applied: reverted batch rotation commit that changed in-flight commit semantics and added normalization of candidate ordering in rerank path (no functional data migration required). Patch rolled to dedicated pool for AtlasSearch in us-west-2 on 2026-03-09. Monitoring shows top-k stabilized and tail-latency returned to baseline. Follow-ups: add unit test for ordering invariants, add metric to alert on partial-commit rate. Ticket will remain open until post-deploy 7-day window completes.
resolution_notes: Patch: PR #2481 reverted and replacement PR #2504 added ordering normalization. Rollout: canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 24h. Post-deploy checks: replayed customer's test suite; 0/100 variance. Schedule: follow-up CI tests and runbook doc update assigned to eng team.
